label: SendGrid
terms_note: Automation allowed: `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` against https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/ (EU-pinned accounts use https://api.eu.sendgrid.com); API keys carry scoped permissions. Rate limits are per endpoint and exposed through X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset (unix ts); 429 for the rest of the window (no per-endpoint numbers on the rate-limit page). Mail Send: POST /v3/mail/send → 202 Accepted; personalizations array ≤1,000; send_at scheduling up to 72 h ahead; categories ≤10 per message (≤255 chars); custom_args ≤10,000 bytes per personalization; dynamic templates `d-…` with Handlebars `dynamic_template_data`; asm.group_id ties the mail to an unsubscribe group (subscription tracking / preferences page); gzip request bodies for high volume. Inbound Parse: MX `mx.sendgrid.net` priority 10 on a dedicated subdomain → multipart/form-data POST (headers, text, html, subject, from, to, envelope, dkim, SPF, spam_score, attachments + attachment-info; or raw MIME `email` field), total message ≤30 MB. Sender identities / domain authentication required before sending.

sdks: Official SendGrid libraries: C#, Go, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby (twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/authentication)

endpoints.call: POST /v3/mail/send` `{personalizations[{to,cc,bcc,subject,headers,custom_args,send_at,dynamic_template_data}], from, reply_to, subject, content[], attachments[], template_id, categories[], custom_args
endpoints.notes: personalizations ≤ 1,000; `send_at` ≤ 72 h ahead; categories ≤ 10 (≤ 255 chars); custom_args ≤ 10,000 bytes / personalization; gzip bodies allowed

endpoints.call: Inbound Parse (MX `mx.sendgrid.net` prio 10 on a dedicated subdomain → `multipart/form-data` POST: headers, text, html, subject, from, to, envelope, dkim, SPF, spam_score, spam_report, attachments + a
endpoints.notes: total message ≤ 30 MB; hostname must not change after creation

endpoints.call: Event Webhook (processed, delivered, deferred, bounce, dropped, spamreport, unsubscribe, group_unsubscribe, open, click; signed)

reference.limits: - Per-endpoint limits exposed as `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` (unix ts); 429 for the rest of the window; no per-endpoint numbers published on the rate-limit page. - Plan-based monthly send volume; sender verification / domain authentication before sending; Twilio acceptable-use policy (no purchased lists) — the suite's consent gate already enforces this.

sandbox.notes: SendGrid has no sandbox host or test key: sandbox mode is the request flag mail_settings.sandbox_mode.enable on POST /v3/mail/send ('validates a Mail Send request without delivering the email'; no Event Webhook or Email Activity events). This adapter does not set that flag, so a send in this environment is a real send; use a restricted API key and your own recipients.

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: SendGrid API key with Mail Send (and, for `me`, User Account read) permission, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <API key>' ('add an HTTP Authorization header to your API request that contains an API Key', https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/authentication). EU-pinned accounts live on https://api.eu.sendgrid.com, which this server does not switch to.

config_fields.name: sender
config_fields.help: Verified sender address used as `from.email` on every send ('from (object with required email field)' — a verified Sender Identity or authenticated domain is required, https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/mail-send/mail-send). Env: PLATFORM_MCP_SENDGRID_SENDER.

adapter.rate_note: 'Each endpoint permits a fixed number of requests per refresh period. If you exceed that limit, the API returns an HTTP 429', announced in X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset (https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/rate-limits); no per-endpoint number is published for mail/send, so the client bucket stays at the runtime default 2/s.

me.note: GET /v3/user/account answers {type: 'free' | 'paid' ('The type of account for this user'), reputation ('The sender reputation for this user')}; there is no richer identity endpoint on the API key itself.

send.note: Sends one plain-text email: `to` is one recipient address (personalizations[0].to[0].email — 'personalizations: An array of messages and their metadata', 'to: array of recipient objects with required email field'), `from.email` comes from the per-install `sender` config field, `subject` is required by SendGrid (a missing subject is a 400 -> isError), `text` is content[0] with type text/plain; `channel` is ignored. SendGrid answers '202 Accepted' with an empty body, so status is the literal 'accepted' and message_id is empty (the id is only in the X-Message-Id response header, which the runtime does not expose).

not_offered.list_inbound: Inbound mail is delivered by the Inbound Parse Webhook (an MX record on a subdomain and a multipart POST to the customer's server), not by a pollable endpoint; the Email Activity API (GET /v3/messages) is a paid add-on with a required query-language parameter (https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/for-developers/parsing-email/setting-up-the-inbound-parse-webhook).
not_offered.get_thread: SendGrid has no conversation or thread resource; sent mail is only queryable through the paid Email Activity API (https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/mail-send/mail-send).
not_offered.reply: A reply would be a new mail/send with In-Reply-To / References headers, but the vocabulary's reply input carries no recipient address and SendGrid has no thread id to resolve one from (https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/mail-send/mail-send).
not_offered.mark_read: No read-state endpoint exists in the SendGrid v3 API (https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference).

evidence: probe: 2/2 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route answered 403 too, so the host authenticates before routing
